Dengue spurt in Thiruvananthapuram: KU’s Karyavattom campus, Cliff House compound emerge as hotspots
 Intermittent spells of rain, followed by hot and humid weather, have led to a spike in dengue cases in Thiruvananthapuram, even as the overall trend in dengue cases across the State has been on a slow decline since July
 Published - November 17, 2026 02:13 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram 
 The Hindu Bureau READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 In the last 10 days, Thiruvananthapuram district has reported 200 probable cases of dengue and 97 confirmed cases.
 | Photo Credit: iStockphoto
 The Karyavattom campus of Kerala University (KU) has emerged as a hotspot of dengue in the city, where over 50 cases have been reported since November 9. Health department suspects that this is a gross underestimation, as the transmission is likely to have begun weeks before
 Intermittent spells of rain, followed by hot and humid weather, have led to the spike in dengue cases in Thiruvananthapuram, even when the general dengue case trend has been on a slow decline since July across the State.
 In the last 10 days, Thiruvananthapuram district has reported 200 probable cases of dengue and 97 confirmed cases.
 Health department cautions against dengue in Kozhikode On Monday, following a meeting called by the Health department, which was joined by the Vice Chancellor, some KU syndicate members as well as public health experts of the School of Public Health under Kerala University of Health Sciences, it was decided to shut the Karyavattom campus and the hostel buildings for three days so that intense vector control measures can be taken up and a break in disease transmission can be achieved.
 “District health officials and vector control teams had visited the campus and hostel and we found that solid waste management was a huge issue in the campus. Plastic disposable containers used for food delivery which are disposed of carelessly are emerging as a major contributor to vector breeding in urban areas.. Rain water stagnation in these containers which are strewn around is a major hazard. Indoor plants in hostel rooms, broken manholes and blocked drains leading to rainwater stagnation have all led to intense mosquito breeding inside the vast campus,” a senior Health official said.
 The Health department has also decided to serve notice to the KU Registrar under the Kerala Public Health Act, for allowing the campus to be a breeding ground for mosquitoes and posing a public health issue
 Epidemic prevention to be strengthened through coordination committees in Keralam Teams from the Pangappara health centre have been at work on the campus since November 10 but the district vector control team and the Corporation health staff will be joining them now. Fogging will be done to kill adult mosquitoes and indoor space spraying inside the hostel room, which will be accompanied by a source reduction campaign, officials said.
 The district health administration has identified several pockets of dengue within the city itself, where an abundance of breeding sources and intense vector breeding has been spotted
 Health officials point out that several large government properties with vast, ill-maintained grounds are also turning out to be hotspots for dengue in the city.
 “The Cliff House compound and the sprawling official bungalows around it are all major breeding grounds for mosquitoes. In the Cliff House, seven police personnel there on guard duty were down with dengue, following which a district health team had visited the location. In some of the bungalows where renovation works are going on, building materials and discarded parts of equipment are all thrown about carelessly, leading to rain water stagnation and mosquito breeding,” a health official said.
 Health officials said that without public participation, source reduction and mosquito control cannot be taken up successfully.
 Kollam district too has reported a significant number of dengue cases over the last 10 days.
 In November so far, the State has recorded 739 confirmed cases and 2,056 probable cases of dengue and three probable dengue deaths.
